output.brief:
The Android login drop is not caused by release 6.14, the Android security patch, or credential-stuffing bots. It started at 10:41 UTC on 3 March, when Corvane's automatic rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17). That rule blocks password logins from the app's networking library when no edge session cookie is present. The block hit every Android version within a minute, including 6.11 to 6.13 that didn't change. Quick-unlock and iOS are unaffected. About 41,300 installs were blocked, and 92% of them had logged in successfully in the previous 90 days, so these are real customers. I'm quite sure of this (about 90%+). The contact-centre call rise is probably partly related, but fee mailings also contributed, so that link is only loosely established.
Next steps: ask Corvane to switch that rule to log-only on the mobile password-login path now, keeping rate limits, lockout and other rules active. Then confirm in telemetry that password success returns to about 96%. Don't roll back 6.14, don't raise bot sensitivity, and don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Those would hide the problem or add more false blocks. Also ask for bank testing or notice of vendor rule changes.
